title: Sales Enablement: Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Decks, Pricing Guidance, Case Studies & Security FAQ
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:

This document is the canonical Redwood Inference sales enablement kit covering: core positioning and messaging, concise competitive briefs and battlecards, pitch deck structure and recommended slides, pricing guidance and examples, two short customer case studies, and a prospect-facing Security & Compliance FAQ. Use this page as the single source of truth for customer-facing collateral and for preparing reps and solution engineers for demos and POCs.

Intended audience:
- Account Executives, SDRs, Solutions Engineers, Sales Engineers, Customer Success Managers, Channel Partners

1) Core positioning and messaging (one-paragraph & three pillars)

One-paragraph positioning:
Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that makes high-performance, predictable LLM serving accessible across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. We help engineering teams ship LLM features with consistent latency, transparent unit economics, and enterprise-grade controls so they can focus on product differentiation instead of running inference infrastructure.

Messaging pillars (use in calls & collateral):
- Production-first performance: predictable latency and throughput — SLOs as low as 50–150ms p50 for typical chat workloads, configurable p95 targets per route.
- Cost-aware controls: batch and cache controls, quantization profiles, and routing policies that reduce per-token cost by up to 3–5x for production workloads.
- Deployment flexibility & security: hosted API for speed, dedicated capacity for SLAs, and private (VPC/on-prem) for regulated data — turnkey integrations with KMS and audit logging.

Buyer personas & tailored hooks:
- Product Engineering (Early-stage/AI-native): focus on quick integration, sample apps, SDKs, and dev UX.
- Platform/Infra Teams (Mid-market/Enterprise): emphasize predictable throughput (Dedicated), autoscaling policies, and observability.
- Security/Compliance Officers: emphasize private deployments, KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, and SOC2-like controls.

2) Competitive brief (top competitors & short differentiation)

Summary table:
Competitor | Typical Strength | Redwood Differentiator
--- | --- | ---
Generic Cloud Provider Endpoints | Large cloud integrations, broad ML ecosystem | Redwood has lighter integration overhead, better token-level cost breakdowns and model-optimized runtime offering lower per-token cost for equivalent latency
Endpoint-focused LLM APIs | Simple interface, rapid TTV | Redwood adds deterministic SLOs, Dedicated capacity, and private deployment options plus advanced batching/caching controls
Self-hosted Inference Runtimes | Full control, lower infra sticker if you operate at scale | Redwood provides the same control surface without the heavy ops burden and includes observability, rollouts, and fallback routing

Top battlecards (one-liners for reps):
- If customer is worried about cost: "We provide model-specific quantization and batching profiles plus a TCO calculator — customers typically see a 2–4x cost reduction versus naive cloud endpoints."
- If customer needs reliability/SLA: "Dedicated capacity and automated fallbacks maintain availability and latency SLOs under load."
- If customer needs private deployment: "We ship a private control plane and on-prem package with KMS/HSM integrations and full audit logging for regulated workloads."

Competitive objections & rebuttals (example):
1) "We can just use cloud vendor managed endpoints."
- Response: "Managed endpoints can be easier initially, but they often lack model-level controls (quantization hints, KV cache management) and fine-grained cost observability. Redwood reduces unit cost and offers Dedicated/Private modes for predictable production economics."

3) Pitch deck — recommended structure (15–20 slides)

Slide outline (minimal notes):
1. Title + one-line value prop
2. Why now? LLM shift and serving complexity
3. Problem statement: unpredictable latency, runaway costs, and ops burden
4. Redwood overview (product modes: Hosted, Dedicated, Private)
5. Core runtime differentiators (batching, KV cache, kernel selection)
6. Developer experience (API/SDK, quickstarts, streaming & tool-calls)
7. Observability & cost transparency (token-level, route dashboards)
8. Reliability & rollouts (canaries, auto-fallbacks)
9. Security & compliance (audit logs, KMS/HSM, VPC)
10. Pricing model summary (hosted per-token, dedicated reserved capacity, private licensing)
11. Case study #1 — Eng-native startup (metrics: latency, cost reduction)
12. Case study #2 — Regulated enterprise (metrics: time-to-deploy private instance, audit readiness)
13. Demo / architecture diagram for POC
14. Integrations & partners (cloud regions, monitoring, KMS)
15. Next steps & pilot offer (technical kickoff checklist)

Deck tips for SEs:
- Start with the customer problem — show measured latency / cost numbers early.
- Use the TCO slide only when the customer expresses cost sensitivity.
- For technical audiences, include a 1-slide runtime architecture with sequence length and kernel selection details.

4) Pricing guidance & examples

High-level pricing constructs:
- Hosted API: usage-based, per-token generation and embedding units. Volume discounts and enterprise rates apply.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU-backed pools (monthly/annual commitments), includes baseline throughput SLA and configurable autoscale policies.
- Private: platform license plus deployment fee and optional support tiers.

Example pricing scenarios (illustrative):
- Early-stage product (100M tokens/mo): Hosted = recommended; estimate $X/month (use TCO calculator for exact numbers).
- Scale SaaS (2B tokens/mo): Consider Dedicated to reduce unit cost; typical savings 30–50% vs hosted at scale due to reserved capacity and quantization profiles.
- Regulated customer: Private deployment with support; pricing includes platform license + deployment + annual support.

Sales negotiation guidance:
- Use credit-based pilots (30–60 days) for proof points.
- Locking on Dedicated requires a minimum N-month commit (see pricing playbook).
- For enterprise deals, offer a technical onboarding package that includes performance tuning and a 2-week on-site/virtual workshop.

5) Case studies (short canonical examples)

Case study A — NovaRetail (AI-native e-commerce startup)
- Problem: Latency-sensitive chat and product search with rising token costs.
- Solution: Moved from cloud endpoints to Redwood Hosted + prefix caching and batching.
- Outcome: p95 latency down 2x; per-token cost reduced ~3x for high-volume reranking pipelines; integration completed in 10 days.

Case study B — FinServCorp (regulated financial services firm)
- Problem: Needed private inference for customer data and audit controls plus predictable throughput.
- Solution: Deployed Redwood Private with KMS integration and dedicated capacity for peak trading hours.
- Outcome: Private deployment completed in 6 weeks; audit logs enabled for internal compliance; SLA-backed latency targets met during peak windows.

6) Security & Compliance FAQ (prospect-facing)

Q: How does Redwood protect customer data in Hosted mode?
A: Hosted API encrypts data in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest. We segregate customer data logically and have role-based access controls across the control plane. For customers with stronger requirements, we recommend Dedicated or Private modes.

Q: Do you offer Private or VPC-isolated deployments?
A: Yes. Redwood Private supports VPC-to-VPC networking, on-prem packaging for air-gapped environments, and a private control plane. We integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key management.

Q: What compliance certifications or evidence do you provide?
A: We maintain internal audit evidence and can provide SOC2-type artifacts on a per-customer basis under NDA. Our security controls map is available at /confluence/security-and-compliance/compliance-evidence-matrix.

Q: How do you handle access controls and audit logging?
A: RBAC for the console and APIs, SSO integrations (SAML/OIDC), and audit logs that record token-level usage and config changes. Logs can be streamed to customer SIEMs where required.

Q: Do you support customer-owned keys?
A: Yes — KMS integrations are available for Dedicated and Private deployments. We also support HSM-based key storage for higher assurance.

7) Demo & POC playbook (technical kickoff checklist)

Pre-demo prep (SE + AE):
1. Collect requirements: target latency, expected tokens/day, security constraints, and desired model(s).
2. Select demo dataset and a 5–10 prompt set that represents production traffic.
3. Provision trial credentials or a dedicated dev instance.

POC timeline (recommended 4 weeks):
- Week 0: Technical kickoff and instrumentation plan.
- Week 1: Baseline measurements against incumbent (latency, cost).
- Week 2: Tune batching/quantization and run performance tests.
- Week 3: Integrate observability dashboards and run regression tests.
- Week 4: Deliver executive summary and recommended deployment mode.

Success criteria to close pilot:
- Achieve target latency (p95/p50) within agreed bandwidth
- Demonstrated unit-cost improvements or predictable cost profile
- Satisfy security requirements for the chosen deployment mode
